question: Why do midwives check the bones and muscles during antenatal visits?

options.A: To measure the exact weight gained during the pregnancy
options.B: To evaluate the internal maturation of the developing fetus
options.C: To diagnose underlying congenital heart defects in the mother
options.D: To distinguish normal pregnancy changes from orthopedic problems

explanation: Midwives perform these assessments mainly to separate expected pregnancy discomforts from actual bone or muscle issues. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do body movements and posture change during pregnancy?

options.A: To allow the maternal pelvic bones to fuse completely early
options.B: To prevent the muscles of the lower limbs from wasting away
options.C: To compensate for a sudden decrease in maternal calcium levels
options.D: To accommodate the growing uterus and prepare for birth

explanation: The body shifts its posture and center of gravity to support the expanding uterus and ready the pelvis for delivery. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h1)

question: What type of information is collected when a client tells a midwife about their joint pain?
explanation: Information reported directly by the patient based on their personal experience is classified as subjective data. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h2)

question: A pregnant client feels severe pain near her pubic bone when walking. What should the midwife ask about next?

options.A: Dietary intake of iron-rich foods and vitamin supplements
options.B: Pelvic girdle discomfort and daily activity limitations
options.C: Frequency of morning sickness and early pregnancy nausea
options.D: Previous history of childhood asthma and respiratory allergies

explanation: Pubic bone pain during walking points directly to pelvic girdle issues, requiring focused questions on mobility and daily strain. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which physical check involves feeling body tissues with the hands to check for tenderness or swelling?
explanation: Palpation uses the hands and fingers to physically examine the texture, temperature, and tenderness of tissues. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why does a midwife compare the left limb with the right limb during an exam?

options.A: To establish a normal baseline for that specific individual
options.B: To check if the skin color matches across the entire body
options.C: To ensure the blood pressure is identical in both arms
options.D: To measure the exact height of the pregnant mother accurately

explanation: Comparing sides helps spot differences or unusual issues unique to that patient. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is it called when a patient moves a joint all by themselves without help?
explanation: Active range of motion refers to movements initiated and completed independently by the patient. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h4)

question: A midwife gently moves a relaxed client's knee through its motion limits while the client rests. What is this called?
explanation: When the examiner moves the relaxed client's joint, it is a passive range of motion assessment. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing joints and ligaments during pregnancy?
explanation: Relaxin is secreted during pregnancy to soften connective tissues and widen the pelvic outlet. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h5)

question: How does an advancing pregnancy usually change the mother's spine shape?

options.A: It creates an abnormal sideways bend known as scoliosis
options.B: It increases lower back inward curvature, known as lordosis
options.C: It flattens the upper back completely into a rigid straight line
options.D: It forces the cervical spine to rotate permanently to one side

explanation: To balance the forward weight of the uterus, the lower spine curves inward, causing pregnancy lordosis. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is keeping accurate notes on bones and muscles important in clinical care?

options.A: It guarantees that the mother will have a normal spontaneous delivery
options.B: It replaces the need to talk directly with the pregnant client
options.C: It ensures safe continuity of care and guides timely referrals
options.D: It eliminates all possible risks of postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Clear notes allow all healthcare team members to track progress and refer clients for specialized care when needed. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h6)

question: What should a midwife do if a pregnant client's back pain makes normal daily movement too difficult?

options.A: Tell the client that all pregnancy back pain must be ignored
options.B: Advise the client to remain completely bedridden for weeks
options.C: Prescribe heavy surgical intervention without consulting a doctor
options.D: Refer the client to a specialist or physiotherapist

explanation: Excessive pain that limits daily life requires professional help beyond routine reassurance. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h6)
